# Shared validator corpus

The privileged helper validates every config twice: once in the app before the
request leaves (`src/main/config-guard.ts`) and once on the root side
(`daemon/internal/guard/guard.go`), because the socket and the one-shot are reachable
by things that are not this app. Both implementations must accept and reject exactly
the same inputs, and this directory is the single fixture set that pins that:
`guard_test.go` reads it here and `src/main/config-guard-corpus.test.ts` reads it
across the tree.

Each `.conf` starts with a header the validators skip as comments:

```
# expect: accept | reject
# reason: not allowed | repeated | missing | malformed | unterminated | outside any section
# why: one line for the reader
```

`reason` is a small stable vocabulary. The Go message must contain it literally; the
TypeScript message is matched by a per-reason pattern in the TS test, because the
TypeScript wording predates the corpus (`must be a number`, `is not a valid key`,
`non-PEM line` all count as `malformed`). Exact text is deliberately NOT compared:
the TypeScript messages echo the offending line, and the Go ones must not (a
one-shot config comes from a caller-supplied path, so an echoed line would be a root
file-read oracle).

`scalars.json` holds the argument validators (IPv4 literal, interface name, SOCKS
address, bypass CIDR, DNS resolver allow-list) as accept/reject lists.

Add a case here whenever a rule changes; the other side's test then fails until it is
mirrored. Regenerated by hand, not by a script.
